summary.text: Marjorie Decker is a Democratic state representative from the 25th Middlesex District who has served since January 2013 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A former Cambridge city councilor, she chairs the Joint Committee on Public Health and has said her priorities include reducing poverty, health care equity and gun safety.

paragraphs.text: Marjorie Decker earned a high school diploma from Cambridge Rindge and Latin High School, a bachelor's degree from the University of Massachusetts Amherst in 1994, and a graduate degree from Harvard's Kennedy School of Government in 2007.
Her prior office was the Cambridge City Council.
In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, she said she grew up in Cambridge public housing and is a mother of two.
Decker assumed office in the Massachusetts House on January 2, 2013.
For 2025-2026 she chaired the Public Health Joint Committee.
In the survey, she said she led the effort to increase the Earned Income Tax Credit from 15% to 40%, authored a maternal health equity law, and passed five gun safety laws.
She advanced from the Democratic primary on September 1, 2026.
